info.name: Festival Management API
info.description:
Backend API for the community festival management app (donations, expenses, tasks, volunteers, multi-colony support). Almost all GET routes are public; every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE route requires a JWT via `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` (see the Auth folder to obtain one).

Colonies have a membership model (see the Colonies folder): creating a colony makes you its first admin, and writes to anything scoped under a colony (its festivals, expected donations, donations tied to an expectation, expenses, expense payments, tasks, task assignments) require the caller to be a member of that colony — a 403 otherwise. `GET /colonies/mine`, `GET /colonies/:id/members`, and `GET /users` are the only GETs in this whole API that require a token, since they expose identity/email/phone data. Managing membership itself (add/change-role/remove) requires being an ADMIN of the colony, not just a member. Walk-in donations (no `expected_id`) and `availability` are NOT colony-scoped. `members` and `donors` are optionally colony-scoped: a `members` row created with a `colony_id` requires colony-admin and lives in that colony's private roster; omit `colony_id` and it behaves as a global, unscoped row same as `donors` always are.

Login identities: `users.email` and `users.phone` are each individually optional (at least one is required) — a self-registered user always has `email` (there is no phone-based self-registration), while a bulk-imported volunteer may have only `phone`. `POST /auth/login` takes exactly one of `email`/`phone` plus `password` — sending both, or neither, is a 400.

Set the `baseUrl` and `token` collection variables before running requests. For the colony-membership and member-login endpoints below, also set `memberUserId` (the target user's numeric id), `memberEmail`, and `memberPhone` — register a second user or bulk-import a member first if you want to test these end-to-end.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Public endpoints — no Authorization header needed. Login here to get the JWT to put in the {{token}} variable for every other request.

request.description: Creates a new user. No auth required. Email+password only — there is no phone-based self-registration; a phone-only login can only be created via Members > Bulk Import Members. Registering alone grants no write access anywhere — a user can only write to a colony's data once they're a member of it (see Colonies > Create Colony, which auto-admins the creator, and Colonies > Add Colony Member for adding others). Returns 201 with `{ user_id, email }` (password hash never included). Duplicate email returns 409.

No auth required. Send exactly one of `email` or `phone` plus `password` — see Login (Phone) for the other form. 400 if `password` is missing or if neither identifier is given; 400 if BOTH `email` and `phone` are given (ambiguous, rejected on purpose). Returns `{ token }` — a JWT valid for 7 days. Copy the token into the collection-level `token` variable so all other requests pick it up automatically. Wrong password and unknown identifier both return 401 with the same message (login intentionally doesn't leak which emails/phones are registered).

Same endpoint and rules as Login (Email), using `phone` instead of `email`. Only accounts created with a `phone` (currently only via Members > Bulk Import Members with `grant_login` set) can log in this way — a plain email/password account has no `phone` set and 401s here.

Requires auth. Self-service password change for the caller's own account — independent of any shared/organizer-set password a bulk-imported member may have been given. `current_password` and `new_password` are both required; 401 if `current_password` doesn't match. Returns 204 with no body.

item.name: Users
item.description: Read-only directory of registered login accounts — used to look up a user's exact `email`/`phone` before adding them to a colony. There is no create/update/delete path here other than Auth > Register and the bulk-import login-granting paths.

query.description: Optional, partial case-insensitive match against email OR phone

request.description: Requires auth (one of only three GETs in this API that do — this data lets you enumerate registered accounts). `search` is optional; omit it to get the full directory (no pagination anywhere in this API). Matches partial, case-insensitive against `email` OR `phone`. Returns `[{ user_id, email, phone }]` — never `password_hash`. Either `email` or `phone` may be `null` on a given row.

item.name: Colonies
item.description: No DELETE endpoint exists for colonies yet — cascade behavior (what happens to festivals under a deleted colony) hasn't been decided, so deletion is deliberately deferred. Colonies have a membership model: creating one makes you its first admin; only members can write data scoped under a colony, and only admins can manage membership or rename/relocate the colony itself.

request.description: Requires auth. Only `name` is required; `location` is optional. The caller automatically becomes this colony's first member, with the `admin` role.
Requires auth. Returns the colonies the caller is a member of, each row including the caller's `role` ('admin' or 'member') in that colony.

query.description: Optional, partial case-insensitive match against name OR location

request.description: Public — no auth required. Returns all colonies ordered by colony_id. Optional `?search=` matches partial, case-insensitive against `name` OR `location`.
Public — no auth required. 404 if the colony doesn't exist.
Requires the caller to be an ADMIN of this colony (not just any member) — 403 otherwise. Partial update — omit any field you don't want to change, it stays as-is (COALESCE semantics).

Requires auth (membership rows expose other users' emails). Does NOT require the caller to be a member of this colony themselves, just logged in. Returns each membership row with the member's `user_id`, `email`, and `role`.

Requires the caller to be an ADMIN of this colony. `email` must belong to an already-registered user (404 if not — there's no invite-by-email-for-strangers flow, and no phone-based equivalent) and must not already be a member of this colony (409 if so). `role` is optional, defaults to `member`; must be `member` or `admin`. Use Users > Search Users first if you only know the person's name.

Requires the caller to be an ADMIN of this colony (checked once for the whole request, not per row). `multipart/form-data`, a `file` field (`.csv` or `.xlsx`/`.xls`, 5MB cap) with columns `email` (required per row — must belong to an already-registered user) and `role` (optional, defaults `member`, must be `member`/`admin`). This grants colony access to people who ALREADY have accounts — for onboarding brand-new volunteers with fresh logins in one step, use Members > Bulk Import Members instead. Returns 201 with `{ created: [...], skipped: [...], errors: [...] }` — `created` rows have the same shape as Add Colony Member's response plus `row` (1-based, data rows only); `skipped` = already a member of this colony; `errors` = unregistered email or a bad `role` value. 400 if no file.

Requires the caller to be an ADMIN of this colony. `role` is required, must be `member` or `admin`. Rejected with 400 if this would demote the colony's last remaining admin — a colony can never end up with zero admins.

Requires the caller to be an ADMIN of this colony. Rejected with 400 if the target is the colony's last remaining admin. There's no self-service "leave a colony" yet — an admin has to remove you. Returns 204.

item.name: Festivals
item.description: current_balance is always computed on read (SUM of matched donations minus SUM of expense_payments) — it is never stored or accepted on PATCH. No DELETE endpoint yet (deferred, same reason as colonies). Writes require the caller to be a member (admin or plain) of the festival's colony — 403 otherwise.

request.description: Requires the caller to be a member of `colony_id`'s colony (403 otherwise). `colony_id`, `name`, and `year` are all required; `colony_id` must reference an existing colony (400 if not).
Public — no auth required. Each row includes a computed `current_balance` field. Optional `colony_id` query param filters to one colony.
Public — no auth required. Includes computed `current_balance`. 404 if not found.
Requires the caller to be a member of this festival's colony (403 otherwise). Only `name` and `year` are updatable — `current_balance` is always derived and silently ignored if sent.

item.name: Members
item.description: Volunteers/organizers directory — distinct from login identity (`users`, see Auth/Users folders), though a member may optionally link to one (see Grant Login below). A member is optionally colony-scoped: omit `colony_id` on create and it's a global, unscoped row writable by any authenticated user (the historical behavior); provide `colony_id` and creation requires that colony's admin, and the row becomes part of that colony's private roster (phone-uniqueness enforced per-colony, not globally). `colony_id` is immutable after creation. No DELETE endpoint yet (deferred).

request.description: Requires auth. `name` is required; `phone` is optional. `colony_id` (optional, not shown in this example body) scopes the row to a colony and requires that colony's admin (403 otherwise) — omit it for the old unscoped-roster behavior, any authenticated user. 409 if `phone` duplicates another row already in that same colony's roster.

Requires the caller to be an ADMIN of `colony_id` (always required here, unlike single-create — a bulk roster upload is inherently "the organizer's own colony"). `multipart/form-data`: `file` (`.csv`/`.xlsx`/`.xls`, 5MB cap), `colony_id` (required), `initial_password` (required, the shared fallback password for any row that grants a login without its own `password` column).

File columns: `name` (required per row), `phone` (required per row — also the dedup key, per-colony only), `email` (optional — non-empty grants a login via email), `password` (optional, overrides `initial_password` for that one row only), `grant_login` (optional — truthy `yes`/`true`/`1`, case-insensitive; only consulted when `email` is empty, grants a login keyed on the row's own `phone` instead). Rows with neither `email` nor a truthy `grant_login` get no login at all — the common "volunteer" case.

Whichever way a login is granted (email or phone), that user is ALSO automatically added to `colony_id`'s membership (role `member`) in the same atomic per-row step — so a freshly bulk-onboarded organizer immediately shows up under Colonies > List My Colonies, no separate Update Colony Role call needed.

Rows are processed independently (one bad row doesn't fail the batch). Returns 201 with `{ created: [...], skipped: [...], errors: [...] }` — `created` rows: `{ row, member_id, name, phone, login_granted, email? }` (`email` present only for the email-granted path). `skipped` = duplicate `phone` within this colony's roster. `errors` = missing `name`/`phone`, `email` already registered, or (phone path) that `phone` already backs another login account globally (`users.phone` is unique across all colonies, unlike the per-colony `members.phone` dedup).

query.description: Optional, partial case-insensitive match against name OR phone; combines with colony_id as AND

request.description: Public — no auth required. Optional `?colony_id=` and `?search=` filters, combinable.
Public — no auth required. 404 if not found.
Requires auth (any authenticated user, regardless of whether the row is colony-scoped). Partial update — only `name`/`phone`; `colony_id` is not PATCH-able (immutable after creation).

Requires colony-admin if this member has a `colony_id`, any authenticated user if it's a legacy unscoped row. Email + password only — this single-grant endpoint was NOT extended to phone (unlike Bulk Import Members, its login-granting code isn't shared with the bulk path), and it does NOT auto-add colony membership the way bulk import now does — a known, flagged inconsistency between the two. `email` and `password` are both required. Returns 201 with the updated member row (`user_id` now set). 409 if the member already has a linked login, or if `email` is already registered to someone else.
Same auth gate as Grant Login. Admin override, no current-password check. `password` is required. 400 if the member has no linked login yet. Returns 200 with `{ member_id, user_id }`.

Promotes/demotes a member (who must already have a linked login) within a colony. 400 if the member has no linked login. Thin dispatcher onto the same logic as Colonies > Add Colony Member / Update Colony Member Role, so it inherits their 403 (not that colony's admin) and 400 (would demote the last admin). `colony_id` and `role` (`member`/`admin`) are both required.

item.name: Donors
item.description: People/entities who pledge or give donations — a global roster with no colony_id, so writes here only require being logged in, not membership in any particular colony. No DELETE endpoint yet (deferred).

request.description: Requires auth. Only `name` is required; `phone` is optional.

Requires auth (any authenticated user — donors are not colony-scoped). `multipart/form-data`, a `file` field (`.csv`/`.xlsx`/`.xls`, 5MB cap) with columns `name` (required per row) and `phone` (optional). No uniqueness constraint on donors at all, so there is no dedup — re-uploading the same file creates duplicate rows. Returns 201 with `{ created: [...], skipped: [], errors: [...] }` — `created`: `{ row, donor_id, name, phone }`; `errors`: missing `name`. `skipped` is always `[]` (kept for response-shape consistency with the other bulk-import endpoints).

query.description: Optional, partial case-insensitive match against name OR phone

request.description: Public — no auth required. Optional `?search=` matches partial, case-insensitive against `name` OR `phone`.
Public — no auth required. 404 if not found.
Requires auth. Partial update.

item.name: Expected Donations
item.description: Pledges tied to a donor + festival. total_donated is computed by summing linked (non-deleted) donations, not stored. No DELETE endpoint yet (deferred). Writes require the caller to be a member of the linked festival's colony — 403 otherwise.

request.description: Requires the caller to be a member of `festival_id`'s colony (403 otherwise). `donor_id`, `festival_id`, `expected_amount`, and `year` are required; `purpose` is optional. `status` defaults to `open` and cannot be set on create.
Public — no auth required. Each row includes a computed `total_donated` field. All query params are optional filters.
Public — no auth required. Includes computed `total_donated`. 404 if not found.

Requires the caller to be a member of this expected donation's festival's colony (403 otherwise). Partial update. `status`, if sent, must be exactly 'open' or 'closed' (400 otherwise) — it is set explicitly, never auto-derived from totals.

item.name: Donations
item.description: Actual money received. Amounts are immutable once created (never edited) — only new rows are added, and delete is a SOFT delete (deleted_at) so history is preserved. If `expected_id` is set, writes require the caller to be a member of that expectation's festival's colony (403 otherwise). Walk-in donations with no `expected_id` are NOT colony-scoped — there's no schema path from a walk-in donation to a colony, so any authenticated user can create/delete those.

request.description: Requires auth. If `expected_id` is set, the caller must be a member of that expectation's festival's colony (403 otherwise). `donor_id`, `amount`, and `date` (YYYY-MM-DD) are required. `expected_id` is optional — omit it for a walk-in donation not tied to any pledge (walk-ins skip the colony check entirely, see folder description). `collected_by` (member id) is also optional.
Public — no auth required. Excludes soft-deleted rows automatically.
Public — no auth required. Returns 404 for a soft-deleted donation, same as if it never existed.

Requires auth; if the donation has an `expected_id`, also requires membership in that expectation's festival's colony (403 otherwise) — walk-in donations skip this check. This is a SOFT delete — sets `deleted_at`, the row and its `amount` are never actually removed or edited. Affects the linked expected_donation's `total_donated` and the festival's `current_balance` on next read. Returns 204 with no body.

item.name: Expenses
item.description: Planned/actual spend against a festival. Delete is a SOFT delete (deleted_at), same rationale as Donations. Writes require the caller to be a member of the linked festival's colony — 403 otherwise.

request.description: Requires the caller to be a member of `festival_id`'s colony (403 otherwise). `festival_id` and `amount_planned` are required; `purpose` and `vendor_name` are optional. `status` defaults to `open`.
Public — no auth required. Each row includes a computed `total_paid` field. Excludes soft-deleted expenses.
Public — no auth required. Includes computed `total_paid`. 404 if not found or soft-deleted.
Requires the caller to be a member of this expense's festival's colony (403 otherwise). Partial update. `status`, if sent, must be exactly 'open' or 'settled' (400 otherwise).

Requires the caller to be a member of this expense's festival's colony (403 otherwise). SOFT delete (deleted_at) — disappears from list/get, feeds into festival `current_balance`. Existing expense_payments under it are NOT cascaded/blocked. Returns 204.

item.name: Expense Payments
item.description: Actual money paid out against an expense. Delete is a SOFT delete — same immutable-money-fields rule as Donations. Writes require the caller to be a member of the linked expense's festival's colony — 403 otherwise.

request.description: Requires the caller to be a member of `expense_id`'s festival's colony (403 otherwise). `expense_id`, `amount`, and `date` (YYYY-MM-DD) are required; `paid_by` (member id) is optional. Note: this is NOT blocked from being created against a soft-deleted expense (a known gap, not yet fixed).
Public — no auth required. Excludes soft-deleted rows.
Public — no auth required. 404 if not found or soft-deleted.

Requires the caller to be a member of this payment's expense's festival's colony (403 otherwise). SOFT delete — affects the parent expense's `total_paid` and the festival's `current_balance` on next read. Returns 204.

item.name: Tasks
item.description: Work items for a festival. Delete here is a HARD delete (unlike money tables) — blocked with a 400 if task_assignments still reference the task. Writes require the caller to be a member of the linked festival's colony — 403 otherwise.

request.description: Requires the caller to be a member of `festival_id`'s colony (403 otherwise). `festival_id` and `title` are required; `planned_date` and `labor_required` are optional. `status` defaults to `planned`.
Public — no auth required.
Public — no auth required. 404 if not found.

Requires the caller to be a member of this task's festival's colony (403 otherwise). Partial update. `status`, if sent, must be exactly 'planned', 'in_progress', or 'done' (400 otherwise, enforced by a DB CHECK constraint).

Requires the caller to be a member of this task's festival's colony (403 otherwise). HARD delete (row is actually removed). Returns 400 if the task still has task_assignments — remove those first via Task Assignments > Delete.

item.name: Task Assignments
item.description: Links a member to a task (volunteer sign-up). HARD delete, no soft-delete concept here. Writes require the caller to be a member of the linked task's festival's colony — 403 otherwise.

request.description: Requires the caller to be a member of `task_id`'s festival's colony (403 otherwise). Both `task_id` and `member_id` are required and must reference existing rows. `signed_up_at` is set automatically (now()).
Public — no auth required.
Public — no auth required. 404 if not found.
Requires the caller to be a member of this assignment's task's festival's colony (403 otherwise). HARD delete. Useful to run before deleting a Task that's blocked by this assignment. Returns 204.

item.name: Availability
item.description: Whether a user is available on a given date. HARD delete, no soft-delete concept here. This table has no festival_id/colony_id at all, so it's NOT colony-scoped by a specific colony — writes here require the caller to be an admin of at least one colony (see Colonies). `(user_id, date)` is unique as of migration 017 — POST (single or bulk) is idempotent: re-posting the same pair updates `is_available` instead of erroring or duplicating the row.

request.description: Requires the caller to be an admin of at least one colony. `user_id`, `date` (YYYY-MM-DD), and `is_available` (boolean) are all required — `is_available` must be a real boolean, not a truthy string. Idempotent on `(user_id, date)`: posting the same pair again updates `is_available` in place instead of creating a duplicate row.

Requires the caller to be an admin of at least one colony (same gate as single Create Availability). Submits multiple dates in one request — built for multi-day festivals (Navratri, Ganesh Utsav) so the client doesn't have to fire one request per day. `user_id` and `is_available` (boolean) are required; `dates` must be a non-empty array of real `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar dates. 400 if `dates` is empty, contains a malformed or nonexistent date (e.g. `2026-02-30`), or `user_id` doesn't reference an existing user. Returns 201 with the array of created/updated rows (same shape as single Create Availability), ordered by `date`. Each `(user_id, date)` pair is upserted — an existing row for that date has its `is_available` updated rather than a duplicate being created.
Public — no auth required.
Public — no auth required. 404 if not found.
Requires the caller to be an admin of at least one colony. `is_available` (boolean) is required — this endpoint only updates that field.
Requires the caller to be an admin of at least one colony. HARD delete. Returns 204.

item.name: Health
item.description: Simple DB connectivity check, not part of the resource API.

request.description: Public — no auth required. Returns `{ status: 'ok', db: 'connected' }` or a 500 with the DB error message.
